notes.title: Herbals Tycoon Developer's Note 01
notes.content: [p]After the release of Version 0.5.1 on March 31 this year, the Early Access (EA) phase of [i]Herbals Tycoon[/i] has come to a temporary close. We are now hard at work developing the full release version. During this process, we will dedicate ourselves to learning Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) knowledge, which will serve as the [b]core gameplay pillar[/b]—rebuilding the original superficial, weak progression-focused gameplay of a pure TCM clinic management sim.[/p][p]This project has had a rocky journey to its current state, undergoing three major overhauls. When I joined the team in 2024, I noticed flaws in the previous development workflow: the gameplay loop had not been finalized, yet most of the assets were already complete. This included character sprites, clinic departments, three growth stages for herbs in the medicine garden, tools for slicing and processing herbs, and even the opening cutscene (a paper-cut animation). However, the script was written in the style of an AVG (Adventure Visual Novel), with excessive scenes, actions, and long, rigid dialogue. Instead of a TCM story, it read more like a wuxia (martial arts) tale—(we may share excerpts from this earlier script someday). At the time, the project’s founder (now my co-founder) had only one year of funding left, so there was extreme urgency to launch.[/p][p]As a result, my entire 2024 was spent on one task: using the assets left by the previous producer to build a playable game framework from scratch. I repurposed pre-existing characters, herbs, and management assets to create a functional prototype. Both Tietou Daba (former editor at [i]TGBUS[/i]) and I are lifelong fans of simulation games—growing up, we loved titles like [i]Theme Hospital[/i], [i]Paladin’s Inn[/i], [i]Chinese Inn[/i], [i]Stardom[/i], [i]Convenience Store[/i], and [i]Uncharted Waters[/i]. You’ll notice [i]Herbals Tycoon[/i] weaves in mechanics from many of these:[/p][list][*][p]Separating diagnosis and treatment rooms (inspired by [i]Theme Hospital[/i]),[/p][/*][*][p]Special visitor events during management (from [i]Chinese Inn[/i]),[/p][/*][*][p]Random resource generation during exploration (from [i]Paladin’s Inn[/i]),[/p][/*][*][p]Dispatchable tasks (from [i]Stardom[/i]),[/p][/*][*][p]Business planning systems (from [i]Convenience Store[/i]),[/p][p]and more.[/p][/*][/list][p]Yet after completing the EA version, we realized a critical flaw: [b]simply “stitching” mechanics together wasn’t fun[/b]. Merging systems we loved as kids made the game overly complex and unfocused. Fortunately, we secured seed funding this year. After carefully listening to feedback from EA players, we made a painful but necessary decision: to [i]rebuild the project from the ground up[/i]. We concluded that patching the EA framework would never fully improve the game’s educational value or fun factor.[/p][p]I previously worked in game development at a major studio, but I only started learning game design when I took over this project—and quickly realized it’s a far deeper discipline than I imagined. In my view, the EA version of [i]Herbals Tycoon[/i] had two key issues:[/p][olist][*][p][b]Lack of conceptual integrity[/b]: The design 思路 was disjointed. While clinic management was meant to be the core, all playable components felt isolated—they failed to integrate with the game’s fundamental concepts or serve the core loop effectively.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Insufficient TCM educational value[/b]: Initially, we worried that incorporating in-depth TCM knowledge would raise the barrier to entry, overwhelming players unfamiliar with the subject. So we created a more superficial clinic management experience. However, after launch, we discovered most players bought the game [i]because[/i] they were interested in TCM education. This motivated our team to dive deeper into TCM studies.[/p][/*][/olist][p]Through this learning, we realized TCM’s core lies in [b]meridians[/b] (energy channels). Even herbs work by targeting specific meridians (a concept called [i]guijing[/i], or “meridian tropism”). In the EA version, meridians were reduced to a trivial mini-game for memorizing head and hand acupoints—with almost no connection to TCM’s actual mechanisms. After much deliberation, we decided to refocus the game:[/p][list][*][p][b]Core gameplay[/b]: Meridians, and how herbs (via [i]guijing[/i]), massage, and acupuncture influence them.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Secondary gameplay[/b]: Clinic management and exploration.[/p][/*][/list][p]This means a complete overhaul of the [i]Herbals Tycoon[/i] project. For now, no further updates will be made to the EA version. However, once the rebuilt version is ready for playtesting, we will move the current EA build to a separate Steam branch (so players can still access the old version) and release the new rebuilt version.[/p][p]I aim to release a demo of the rebuilt version before the Lunar New Year. It will be available for free on the [i]Herbals Tycoon[/i] Demo page on Steam.[/p][p]Thank you all for your support of the [i]Herbals Tycoon[/i] project and our team![/p][p][/p][p]By Huang Gaole, Producer[/p]

notes.title: The Veteran Chinese Medicine Practitioner Officially Starts Business!!!
notes.content:
[h2]Dear players,[/h2]

Hello everyone! Through the unremitting efforts of the development team, we are delighted to announce that Herbal Pathways was officially launched in its Early Access (EA) version on the Steam platform at 15:00 on January 17, 2025!

EA Price: 42 yuan (The price may increase for the full - version)
Launch Discount: 10%
Final Price: 37.8 yuan

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3014680/_/


This is an adventure that combines Chinese - style aesthetics with traditional Chinese medicine. You can immerse yourself in the ancient charm, learn about herbal knowledge, manage a traditional Chinese medicine clinic, and experience diverse gameplay. Although we are still inexperienced, we are full of enthusiasm and do our best to optimize. If there are any shortcomings in the initial version, please be understanding. Your feedback is the driving force for our progress. Thank you very, very much for your support.

notes.title: A Letter from the Producer to the Players
notes.content:
Dear players,

Hello everyone. The Early Access (EA) version of Herbal Pathways has finally met you. It is an EA version because our work is not yet complete, and neither the degree of completion nor the quality has reached the level that satisfies us. However, we still hope you can give us more support. The suggestions and opinions of every player in the EA version will be crucial reference information for us to continue to complete the game in the new year.

The entire R & D process has been both painful and enjoyable. The theme of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) is indeed challenging. It's not only about production and planning but also about understanding TCM. This requires long - term collection of reference materials and comparison of various information. Eventually, we chose an alternate history setting, hoping that during the whole gameplay process, while bringing joy to players who like it, we can popularize some of the culture left by our ancestors.
PS: Please remember, do not buy herbs and boil them at home to test the medicine on yourself. Remember this firmly, Σ(⊙▽⊙"a.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45138873/0c96882706d72e58cc2db3348d7cafbf8c1dd7ce.png[/img]

[h2]Completed parts of Herbal Pathways currently:[/h2]
The large - cycle logic of the gameplay structure is complete, allowing for a complete playthrough experience.
The appearance conditions and plot of 15 main story characters have been presented, and introductions to the main medical schools and the background of the worldview have all been revealed.
The first 5 achievements of the game have been released.

[h2]Unsatisfactory parts of Herbal Pathways currently:[/h2]
The game guidance is not detailed. Almost all management elements are presented at the beginning, and players need to explore on their own. Many gameplay modules still need to be further refined.
The main and side storylines have not been fully designed yet. Therefore, many ideas related to the plot that can affect the game flow experience in the later stage of the game have not been integrated into the game. You may start to feel bored in the second half of the game.
The popularization of TCM is still rather superficial. It has not achieved the original intention of teaching through entertainment. The basic theories, physiology, causes of diseases, diagnostic methods, treatment principles of TCM, as well as the composition and application of prescriptions and medicines, and the popularization of the twelve meridians have not been well integrated into the game elements.
We don't have a professional testing position, so you may encounter some incredible bugs at any time during the game.
If you encounter bugs during the game, please feel free to contact us:
Or the Steam discussion area

If you are a user of other languages (English, Japanese, Korean), you may find that some parts such as names or proper nouns in the game have not been translated yet. If there are untranslated contents that hinder the normal understanding and gameplay of the game, please be sure to let us know in the comments. We plan to complete the multi - language translation and adaptation of all UI elements by February 28th.

Finally, thank you for your purchase. We will definitely work harder to update in 2025 and strive to release the full version in about 12 months.

notes.title: The new product festival has been launched, everyone hurry up
notes.content:
[b]Dear herbal masters[/b]


The book 'Returning to the Origin of Materia Medica' has been launched on Steam with our beloved herbs! Now you can try our demo for free, won't you come and give it a try?

This is not a typical simulation business game! Here, you can grow medicine, treat diseases, and open a clinic. While playing, you can also secretly learn a lot of traditional Chinese medicine knowledge, which will definitely make you a "health expert" in your social circle and never become an unknown expert. (Insulated cups are not included)



You will play the role of an ancient medicine shop owner, personally preparing medicinal herbs and diagnosing the illnesses of various heroes in the martial arts world! Don't worry, you don't need to really understand medical skills, but you must be able to 'prescribe'! Come and challenge yourself, see if you can become the backbone of the clinic!



In the trial, not only is the content extremely interesting, but we also hope that you can provide some valuable feedback! We accept both good and bad, let's work together to make this game better and better. Otherwise, it would be difficult to match the prescription with just a few words from us!



Player QQ group: 933369664



are you ready? The door to the world of herbs has opened, it's up to you to prepare the medicine!

notes.title: Update on October 1st
notes.content:
[h1] Update: [/h1]

1. Increase patient action flow animations and provide feedback during management, such as gift bubbles and referrals to other clinics.
2. Parameter adjustment, attempting to solve the following problems: skyrocketing and plummeting reputation; Making money is difficult, and high prices of medicinal herbs can result in losses. The construction materials and departmental parameters have also been optimized and adjusted.
3. Set page optimization to adjust resolution and window mode. You can return to the game main menu through the system menu.
4. Add a broadcasting system to the business interface to view details of abnormal operations in the hospital.
5. Add randomly generated physicians to prevent the recruitment of physicians in the talent pool from happening too quickly.
6. Targeted collection of construction materials can be carried out in the medicine garden.
7. The prescription has been reviewed, and the dosage and processing method of the medicinal materials have been revised according to the "Pharmacology".
8. Replace character materials with refined ones.
9. The difficulty of overseas assignments is reduced. Chen Tianming completing an overseas mission can unlock Bai Jimin.
10. GameOver ending with increased fiscal deficit.

notes.title: The demo playtest will begin on August 16th at 16:00.
notes.content:
We are thrilled to announce that Herbals Tycoon will begin its first demo playtest on August 16th at 16:00! During this test, you will have the opportunity to experience the core gameplay and content for the very first time.

While we are aware that the current version still has some shortcomings, such as the completeness of content, accuracy of proofreading, and the absence of certain story elements, we believe that by involving more players, we can better gather valuable feedback and suggestions to continuously improve the game experience.

As a game focused on the dissemination of traditional Chinese medicine, we understand the challenges this subject presents. Traditional Chinese medicine is profound and vast, and integrating it into a game while conveying it to a broad audience is no easy task. However, we are committed to our deep respect and passion for this rich cultural heritage. We strive to do our best within our capabilities to create a game world that is both deep and engaging.

We sincerely hope that you will share your thoughts, experiences, and suggestions, helping Herbals Tycoon improve through our collective efforts.

Thank you to every player who supports us. Your support gives us the motivation to keep moving forward.

We look forward to seeing you in the world of Herbals Tycoon!

notes.title: Developer's self description
notes.content:
[b] Dear player friends: [/b]
 
 
hello everyone! Today, I would like to share with you the story behind the game "Ben Cao Gui Yuan Lu".
In January 2020, we participated in a national cultural and creative talent training course (Traditional Culture Inheritance and Innovation Direction) held in Fuzhou City, Jiangxi Province. During this period, due to convenient conditions (organized by the organizer), we visited medical history memorial halls such as Xujiang Medical and Jianchang Gang, and learned about some basic information about traditional Chinese medicine, including some famous local doctors such as Chen Ziming, Gong Tingxian, Li Ting, etc. Soon after, there was a mask problem in Wuhan, which caused panic nationwide, and medical supplies became extremely scarce. There is a scene where Tan Ju and his lover Director Ai from the Fuzhou Municipal Bureau of Culture and Tourism are on duty in the community every day, delivering traditional Chinese medicine and ingredients door-to-door. Even now, we still cannot forget this scene when we recall it. We know what we need to do now. We have experienced the "sincerity of great doctors" from ancient times to the present, the unique theory and medical practice of traditional Chinese medicine, and the outstanding contributions of this traditional Chinese medicine culture that has been born and bred on the land of China for thousands of years to life, health, and disease.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45138873/c505f24b09b3e75b66a10d3ebfe04542a362a147.jpg[/img]

We believe that the spirit of excellent doctors should be worthy of praise in any era, whether it is modern medicine or traditional medicine. That's why we have decided to create a game for traditional Chinese medicine, using the form of a game to popularize the relevant understanding and viewpoints of traditional Chinese medicine

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45138873/6d20d17ab0f17416166e4f45e72c434b45090f9e.jpg[/img]
 
Most of our team members come from the Orange Light gaming field. For example, our boss previously trained original artists for the Orange Light game material library, and the producer is a contracted author of Orange Light. Therefore, the art style of our works naturally carries the genes of Orange Light style. We hope to strive towards the perspective of Chinese style and realistic Chinese style (the art style has been comprehensively adjusted for at least three editions since its inception, and we also hope that everyone can see this effort). And we have always hoped to make breakthroughs in gameplay, wanting to create a traditional Chinese medicine themed game that is both fun and informative.
 

However, the path of transformation has been exceptionally difficult. Traditional Chinese medicine popularization itself is extremely challenging, while we also need to balance survival and ideals. Ensure that the game can continue to be produced with quality. Over the past three years, some of our former comrades who fought together have left due to unforeseen circumstances, while others have joined with new aspirations. The project has also been suspended and started, taking many detours. The biggest challenge is that there are very few people in the team who have knowledge of traditional Chinese medicine (our previous plan was for Western medicine students at Shanxi Medical University), and the consultants with rich experience in traditional Chinese medicine are not very familiar with game design. This has led to the game being repeatedly overturned and restarted, and even now our understanding of traditional Chinese medicine is inevitably shallow, with errors and omissions. We hope everyone can forgive us and help us correct and correct mistakes. We will humbly and patiently verify and correct them.
 
Now, our work is presented to everyone in the form of simulated management. Although it is still in its early stages with only a complete framework and structure, the support and encouragement from players have filled us with confidence, and we look forward to filling it out together with everyone.

Finally, I hope everyone can support 'The Return of Materia Medica to the Origin' more and work together to make this traditional Chinese medicine themed game better and better!

Thank you again everyone.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45138873/7649d63cd5ca4acc6ff0bfb1d54dbdd6e4168fab.jpg[/img]

If you like it, you can join the group and communicate with us: 933369664 [/h2]
